**Chapter 5**

The Hidden Tab

*Before a file goes out, who checks what is in it that nobody can see?*

On 3 August 2023, the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) received two Freedom of Information requests. Both came from the same person through WhatDoTheyKnow (WDTK), a public website that publishes FOI requests and the answers to them.

To answer, PSNI staff downloaded data from the PSNI's SAP HR system as an Excel file with a single worksheet. While analysing the data for disclosure, they added more worksheets. Before release, they deleted all the visible tabs, but the original worksheet with staff personal details stayed in the file. Quality assurance did not catch it (ICO).

On 8 August 2023, at 14:31, the file was uploaded to WDTK. Around 16:10, PSNI officers alerted the organisation. WDTK hid the file at 16:51, and it was deleted at 17:27 the same day (ICO).

The hidden worksheet listed 9,483 serving PSNI officers and staff. It held surnames, first-name initials, job role, rank, grade, department, post location, contract type, gender, and service and staff numbers (ICO).

John Edwards, the UK Information Commissioner, said later: “The sensitivities in Northern Ireland and the unprecedented nature of this breach created a perfect storm of risk and harm”. He described a “tangible fear of threat to life”.

In September 2023, the ICO issued an advisory note to public authorities on keeping personal information out of FOI responses.

On 11 December 2023, the PSNI and the Northern Ireland Policing Board published an independent review, “Protecting from Within”. It was led by Temporary Commissioner Pete O'Doherty, the National Police Chiefs' Council lead for Information Assurance and Cyber Security. It was an “end to end process review”, and it made 37 recommendations under five headings.

On 23 May 2024, the ICO announced that it intended to fine PSNI £750,000. It said PSNI's “internal procedures and sign-off protocols” for disclosing information safely were inadequate. Edwards called the breach avoidable. He said “simple and practical-to-implement policies and procedures would have ensured” it did not happen. Without the ICO's approach to fining public bodies, the fine would have been £5.6 million.

The same day, mySociety, which runs WDTK, said it had built a tool that checks spreadsheets arriving as FOI answers and holds back files that seem to contain hidden data. In its first three months, the tool screened 3,064 files. It stopped 21 spreadsheets confirmed to contain data breaches and 53 likely to contain them (mySociety).

On 3 October 2024, the ICO issued its final penalty notice: £750,000, for breaching Articles 5(1)(f), 32(1) and 32(2) of the UK GDPR between 25 May 2018 and 14 June 2024. Edwards said: “I cannot think of a clearer example to prove how critical it is to keep personal information safe.” He told other organisations: “Check, challenge and change your disclosure procedures to ensure you protect people's personal information.”

THE RECORD

- Two FOI requests on WhatDoTheyKnow, received 3 August 2023, from the same requester. Requester not named in the record; do not name them.
- The released Excel file, uploaded 8 August 2023 at 14:31, hidden at 16:51, deleted at 17:27. Structure: visible worksheets with the requested figures, plus a hidden original worksheet exported from SAP HR with 9,483 rows of staff data. Show structure only, never contents.
- ICO advisory note to public authorities on FOI disclosures, September 2023. Text not reviewed here.
- “Protecting from Within: a review of the PSNI data breach 8th August 2023”, published 11 December 2023. Led by T/Commissioner Pete O'Doherty. 37 recommendations in five sections: Organisational, Governance and Accountability; Taking Responsibility; Building the Foundations; Data Sharing and Usage; Data Culture, Skills and Talent. Full text not reviewed here.
- ICO notice of intent and preliminary enforcement notice, announced 23 May 2024. Provisional fine £750,000.
- ICO monetary penalty notice, 3 October 2024. £750,000. UK GDPR Articles 5(1)(f), 32(1) and 32(2). Period 25 May 2018 to 14 June 2024.

THE CHAIN

1. FOI requester. Sent two requests through WDTK on 3 August 2023.
2. PSNI staff preparing the response. Exported raw HR data instead of only the figures needed, then added worksheets.
3. PSNI staff preparing the response. Deleted the visible tabs but left the original worksheet in the file. CONTROL POINT. The ICO said the hidden data stayed in the file when all visible tabs were deleted.
4. Quality assurance and sign-off. Did not find the hidden worksheet. CONTROL POINT. The ICO found the “internal procedures and sign-off protocols” inadequate and said “simple-to-implement procedures could have prevented the serious breach”.
5. Upload to WDTK at 14:31 on 8 August 2023.
6. PSNI officers spotted it around 16:10. WDTK hid it at 16:51. It was deleted at 17:27.

WHAT THE RECORD RECOMMENDS

- Edwards: “Check, challenge and change your disclosure procedures to ensure you protect people's personal information.”
- The ICO's preliminary enforcement notice required PSNI to improve the security of personal information when responding to FOI requests.
- In practice: never release a working file. Copy only the figures needed into a new, clean file, or export to a plain format such as CSV. Before release, check for hidden sheets, hidden rows and columns, and source data, and have a second person sign off.

CAUTIONS

- No names of the staff who prepared the response. No names of the requester. No data from the leaked file, not even an example row.
- Some reports say the file was online about 2.5 hours. Use the ICO's times: uploaded 14:31, hidden 16:51, deleted 17:27.
- Reports that the data reached dissident republicans were not verified from these sources. Leave them out.
- The independent review's own text was not read. Use only its title, date, lead, the figure of 37 recommendations and the five section headings.
- Do not blame WDTK. The record places responsibility on PSNI's procedures.

ELSEWHERE

- Morgan Stanley, October 2017: an IT consultant found MSSB customer data on drives bought at auction (see Chapter 4). [6]

FROM THE COURSE DECK

The SecureTree.ai CISSP deck, quoted exactly. Lessons may quote these lines and cite the slide.

- Slide 99: “Sensitivity: Loss if information is revealed to unauthorized individuals.”
- Slide 112, Data Owner: “Approve or deny data disclosure requests.”
- Slide 122, Separation of Duties: “Distributes critical tasks among multiple individuals.”
